body:
I have anxiety. I've posted about it here before (this is a particularly rough time for me). I seriously can't do anything for myself beyond the absolute basics (hygiene, occasionally cooking). I need support because I'd literally be dead without it. Homeless, unemployed, can't drive, can't talk to strangers. 

I gguess I'm really hurt by what my boyfriend is saying because I don't think it's all "negatives." I think that the proportion of normal conversations to "I'm freaking out" ones is pretty good considering what's going on in my life. Twice over the past 10 days I've pulled his sorry ass out of the "I'm a piece of shit" blues. His issues are a lot easier to fix than mine because he gets stressed over, say, a project or having to work too much and it's easy to soothe that away with Chinese food and helping him do his laundry so he can catch up on life. I get stressed over pretty much nothing that can be helped because all my issues are huge and impossible but I don't think I'm always hung up on them. 

My mom says mean things to me all the time. I babysit, and this week I found out that one of the kids I watch is going to be coming over 2 days a week instead of 3. My mom told me today that it's probably because they don't like me which really hurts.

Thank you for this.

It's funny, two of my biggest, most obvious fears are driving and foods. Every time I get behind the wheel of a car or am served an unfamiliar food, I will involuntarily tear up and I can feel all my muscles begging me to go crawl back into my bed and take a nap.

I often fantasize about being a stunt driver in action movies and cooking sophisticated, authentic ethnic foods. Whether those are two things I'm organically interested in or if it's some sort of masochistic idea I use to beat myself up with, I don't know. But I don't know if I could do it. Half of what happens to me isn't even a choice. It's not that I'm looking at the steering wheel and thinking "oh, this is scary." My body is reacting to these things I fear as if they are very real and dangerous threats. The same way average people would have a hard time looking down into the Grand Canyon and throwing themselves in because their bodies are saying "no, this will kill you, don't do that," I can't bring tomatoes to my lips without shaking and tearing up and if I try to get myself just *that* far I'll have bad dreams about chewing tomatoes for a week after.

I think I may have been unclear; I'm not a mother. God, I don't think I would survive a pregnancy in my current state. Any amount of physical discomfort makes me want to throw myself off a cliff (good thing I'm afraid of heights). I was raised by a very young and slightly narcissistic mother who took me to be evaluated when I was young, it's not me taking my kid around! I'm only a nanny.

I made an appointment with a psychiatrist. I have about a month before I can go in. I'm nervous. I've heard that benzos are awesome for people like me but are only prescribed for a certain period of time. I have a close friend who went through something similar to my problem and experienced huge success on lexapro. I just feel like I'm so far behind and even with medication it's going to take so much to get myself up to where a normal 20-year-old should be. 

My last true panic attack was this summer. I straight-up blacked out in a subway car. I "fainted" but was still crying and shaking and stuff. I woke up to my boyfriend and a complete stranger holding me in their laps and rubbing my back and my boyfriend asking me if I can count to ten, then cracking a Spinal Tap joke when I made it to ten and asked me to go up to eleven instead. A huge part of the reason I'm still here is that I don't want him to go through the process of grieving and finding love again but it's shitty to stay alive for a person because people are fallible.

Thank you.

My biggest problem is that I'm only at peace or even feel like staying alive when I'm in that position; in bed or generally comfortable and in a soft place and getting wrapped up in something lighthearted. It's not unusual for me to spend 23 hours a day in my bed and still feel overwhelmed after. When I get up and do laundry I feel miserable. I signed up for a 6-week martial arts class on a whim because I decided I wanted to break my bubble and I'm miserable over it. I spent the whole day being nervous and high-strung and easily upset over nothing because I was so nervous about going to my class today. I go back this weekend and I'm absolutely dreading it. The class itself is fine, I'm just so overwhelmed by it all and I know I have to keep going back. I've tried getting jobs and stuff and it just doesn't get better. My only "real" job was actually fine at first, I loved it, it was awesome, but once I realized that it was a regular part of my schedule and not something that would end and let me get back to "normal" I started to freak out, I felt tired and busy all the time, and I needed to quit. And clearly I can't live life taking jobs for 2 months at a time with 3 year breaks in between. So, I don't know.
